report.title: Rajwinder Singh: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: There is no mandatory ACCT refresher training for prison officer at HMP Wandsworth
concerns.hazard: lack of mandatory ACCT refresher training for prison officers

concerns.quote: There are no mandatory procedures to ensure that, before they are deployed in the prison setting, Oxleas agency staff have the same mandatory ACCT training as that provided to permanent healthcare staff
concerns.hazard: lack of mandatory procedures for Oxleas staff ACCT training parity

concerns.quote: When Prison Officers and/or Healthcare staff are given ACCT induction training at HMP Wandsworth, there is no training in the principles of risk formulation
concerns.hazard: lack of risk formulation training in ACCT induction

earlier.title: Jack Zarrop: Prevention of future deaths report

matches.explanation: Both reports highlight that agency healthcare staff in prisons are not receiving mandatory ACCT training comparable to permanent staff. This gap creates a risk of inadequate suicide and self‑harm prevention.

report.title: Claire Driver: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: there were only two attempts to see Claire by the enhanced community mental health team between 28 November 2023, when she was seen in police custody, and 16 January 2024, when she was detained under the Mental Health Act, despite clear evidence her mental health was deteriorating
concerns.hazard: lack of engagement with mental health services

concerns.quote: training on the effect of substance misuse on mental health conditions is not mandatory for all staff and would be of assistance when caring for patients such as Claire
concerns.hazard: inadequate staff training on substance misuse impact
